messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated error rate detected on serving-runtime-us-west-2. Metric: cuda_illegal_memory_access rate = 7.1% (baseline 0.02%). Trigger: 5xx/cuda-exceptions. Paging #incidents and #eng-oncall.

alice: I'm investigating — seeing a restart loop on gpu-node-47. Containers repeatedly crash with cudaErrorIllegalAddress and then OOM-kill sometimes, followed by kernel oops mentioning a pagewalk/unaligned address. Pulling full logs now.

ben: can we cordon gpu-node-47 to stop new scheduling? I'll start evacuations for inference pods.

alice: doing cordon/drain now. commands I ran:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-47
kubectl drain gpu-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
drain in progress, a few pods are stuck terminating (nvml-exporter, model-runtime).

alice: raw crash snippet from model-runtime on gpu-node-47: 
```
I0325 14:11:02.123 model-runtime[1]: ERROR: cuda runtime error (77) : an illegal memory access was encountered at /workspace/runtime/src/cuda_kernels.cu:452
I0325 14:11:02.124 model-runtime[1]: Backtrace:
#0 0x7f8a2b3c in serve_loop
#1 0x7f8a2b9d in dispatch_batch
#2 0x7f8a2c4f in kv_cache_apply
KernelOops: page_walk_fault addr=0x7fff1a2b offset=0x10 (misaligned pagewalk)
```
Noting both user-space illegal access and kernel pagewalk log entry within same second.

dmitri: this looks like a race during page table updates combined with eviction — we've seen similar when large KV-cache allocations and preemption collide. Two immediate mitigations: 1) evacuate the node (cordon/drain) and reboot if kernel oops persists; 2) reduce batcher_max_tokens and disable local KV cache on the model-runtime to avoid large device allocations.

ben: cordon complete. evicted most pods. One pod showing CrashLoopBackOff with containerd error before kernel log: "containerd: non-zero exit (SIGSEGV)". Reboot queued for gpu-node-47 after we finish evacuations.

eve: customer-impact snapshot: ~12 active customers had >=10% error rates over last 10m; p99 latency doubled for several realtime routes. Tiered fallbacks triggered for paid customers but free-tier experienced delays. Recommend a short customer notice and ops status update if we can't fully mitigate in 30m.

alice: rolled back the recent runtime build on the serving fleet as a canary hotfix to v1.24.1 (we had pushed v1.24.2 this morning). Rollout command: 
```
redwood ctl rollout rollback --service serving-runtime --to v1.24.1 --namespace prod --concurrency 5
```
I also pushed a runtime flag to disable KV caching on the active canary group: `--kv-cache=off` and reduced `--batcher-max-tokens=512`. Monitoring for error-rate drop.

dmitri: good. also reduce node-level eviction aggressiveness for a short window to avoid thrash (set eviction threshold to 0.9 rather than 0.7) and temporarily route new low-latency traffic to cpu-variant endpoints until we confirm stability. I'll open a firewall rule to prefer cpu nodes for the next 45m.

ben: gpu-node-47 rebooted after kernel oops; hardware reports ECC errors on one GPU PCIe lane. Opening a ticket with infra/hardware and marking node for deeper diag. Replaced the node from the pool (new-node-89) and rebalanced pods.

alice: error-rate dropped to 0.6% in the last 5m after rollback+kv-off+batch reduction. Still above baseline but trending down. Can we keep the canary running for 30m then promote if stable?

dmitri: yes — keep canary for 30m. Also filing a follow-up: reproduce plan to stress the pagewalk by combining large-batch inference + eviction churn. Assigning to eng-runtime for deeper kernel-level trace.

ben: escalation note — paging eng-runtime@pagerduty and kernel-team@pager for postmortem. I've added preliminary logs to the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/5100001234 (draft).

eve: I'll draft a short customer status: note that some realtime requests experienced errors, we've rolled back a runtime change and mitigations are in place; ETA for next update 30m. Posting to status.redwood.ai once we confirm stability.

alice: handoff: I'm heading OOO in 20m; ben — can you continue watch and escalate if error-rate creeps above 2%? dmitri — please take the technical lead for postmortem.

ben: ack, taking watch. summary for handoff -> dmitri: root cause suspected: interaction between recent runtime change (v1.24.2) that changed allocation pattern and kernel pagewalk race during eviction resulting in cudaErrorIllegalAddress and kernel pagewalk oops. Current mitigation: rollback to v1.24.1, disable kv-cache, lower batcher tokens, cordon+reboot affected node, replace hardware if ECC persists. Logs and runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/serving-runtime-cuda-illegal.

ben: handing off at 5100004834 to dmitri (oncall). dmitri — you're up for postmortem and customer comms until resolution is stable. :thumbsup:

eng-runtime: follow-up tasks created: [RT-4251] reproduce env + kernel-trace, [RT-4252] investigate v1.24.2 allocator diff, [RT-4253] hardware diag for gpu-node-47.

incident-bot: Incident status changed -> mitigated (partial). Monitoring.

alice: thanks everyone — closing loop on immediate ops, will join postmortem later.

(threads/traces attached to incident doc: kernel logs, container logs, rollout commands, evacuation timeline)
